To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The optimal server size is determined by the ratio of the service charge to the cost of energy; 2) The optimal server speed is determined by the service-level agreement and the penalty of a poor-quality service.
the optimal number of servers is a function of the service charge, and the optimal server configuration is a function of both the service charge and the business cost.
the optimal server size depends on the service-level agreement and the service charge, and the optimal server size is independent of the server speed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal configuration of a multiserversystem in cloud computing, such that a service provider can maximize the profit.
the optimal multiserver configuration in a cloud computing setting.
the optimal configuration for profit maximisation in a cloud computing system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal server configuration for profit maximizations depends on the server speed and power models, the service level agreement, the penalty of service failure, and the cost of server energy consumption.

the optimal server size is not always equal to the number of service requests per unit of time, and that the optimal server speed depends on the server size, the service-level requirement, the penalty for a low-quality service and the service charge.
the optimal server speed and size are determined by the service charge of an individual service request, the cost of server renting, and the cost of server power consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model and approach provide a useful tool to help a cloud computing service provider to understand the economics of cloud services, and to maximize the profit.
we are able to derive a mathematical expression for the expected net business gain and the expected profit, and we can solve for the optimal server size analytically.

we have provided a theoretical foundation to help cloud service providers to make optimal decisions on the configuration of a server system for maximizing their profits, and to help cloud service consumers to make informed decisions on the selection of a server system and its configuration for minimizing the service charge and maximizing the quality of a cloud service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal server speed is not always the highest possible, but depends on the service charge, the business cost, the server size, and the server speed.

the optimal server size for profit maximization is determined by the ratio between the service charge and the cost per server per unit time, and the optimal server size is not necessarily equal to the maximum server size.
a service provider can maximize his or her profit by choosing the appropriate server size and server speed.
